grits-instant-made-with-water-no-added-f.title: Grits, instant, made with water, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Grits are finely ground corn kernels designed for quick preparation. When hot water is added, they form a smooth, slightly creamy porridge without any added fat. The product is often used as a fast breakfast or side dish.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Grits are made from whole corn, one of the world’s oldest cultivated crops.
Instant grits appeared in the United States in the mid‑20th century as a convenient food for soldiers and travelers.
Corn provides carotenoids that give grits their characteristic yellow hue.
Grits are a staple in traditional Southern dishes such as “shrimp and grits.”
When prepared correctly, grits retain most of the corn’s dietary fiber.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Grits supply slowly digestible energy, helping to maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Corn fiber supports digestive health and promotes satiety.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes grits suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Source of iron
items.content: Corn provides iron, essential for oxygen transport in the blood.

items.title: Corn allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to corn products.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Grits have a relatively high GI, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Sodium content in flavored mixes
items.content: Some ready‑to‑eat versions contain added salt; choose unsalted varieties if sodium intake is a concern.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Combine 1 part grits with 3–4 parts hot water, stir, and let stand for 2–3 minutes. Add fruit, berries, nuts, honey, or spices to taste.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store grits in a cool, dry place in an airtight container. After opening, use within 3–4 months for best quality.

content.title: About
content.content: Kibby is a fragrant blend of dried fruits, nuts, and spices inspired by traditional Puerto Rican sweets. It combines the sweetness of mango, pineapple and coconut with a subtle hint of cinnamon and clove, creating a bright and rich flavor profile.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The Kibby recipe is based on generations‑old Puerto Rican family traditions.
Dried mango, considered the "golden fruit" in Puerto Rico for its color and taste, is a key ingredient.
Kibby is traditionally sold in small portion packets for holidays and family gatherings.
The mix of nuts and spices makes it a natural source of quick energy for active people.
Kibby contains no artificial colors or flavorings.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: The dried fruits and nuts provide vitamin B6 and niacin, which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of healthy fats
items.content: Nuts supply monounsaturated fats that are beneficial for heart health.

items.title: Contains dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber from the dried fruits aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Coconut and spices such as cinnamon and clove are rich in antioxidants that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin C from dried pineapple boosts the immune system.

items.title: Tree nut allergy
items.content: The product contains nuts, which may trigger allergic reactions in sensitive individuals.

items.title: High natural sugar
items.content: Dried fruits are naturally sweet, so people monitoring blood sugar should consume Kibby in moderation.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: The blend is calorie‑dense; portion control is recommended, especially on weight‑management diets.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Some versions may contain a small amount of salt for flavor; those with hypertension should check the label.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Enjoy Kibby as a snack on its own, stir it into yogurt, oatmeal, smoothies, or use it in baked goods. For a softer texture, soak the dried fruits in warm water for 10‑15 minutes before eating.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store Kibby in an airtight container in a cool, dry place away from direct sunlight. For longer shelf life, keep the package in the refrigerator to preserve flavor and prevent the nuts from going rancid.

content.title: About
content.content: Malted milk is a dairy beverage to which malted barley extract has been added. It has a mildly sweet, caramel‑like flavor and a creamy texture. The product is widely used in cooking, for desserts, shakes, and as a base for infant nutrition.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The malt extract gives the milk a characteristic golden hue.
Malted milk is a traditional ingredient in many Scandinavian recipes.
The lactose content may be slightly higher than in regular milk because of the added maltose.
It is often served chilled in summer and warm in winter.

items.title: Source of calcium
items.content: Like regular milk, malted milk provides calcium essential for strong bones and teeth.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Maltose contributes riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which support energy metabolism.

items.title: Supports immunity
items.content: Vitamin D and vitamin A present in the milk help maintain immune function.

items.title: Energy source
items.content: The combination of lactose and maltose offers both quick and sustained energy.

items.title: Contains protein
items.content: Milk proteins (casein and whey) aid in tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Lactose intolerance
items.content: People with lactose intolerance should limit intake or choose lactose‑free alternatives.

items.title: Milk protein allergy
items.content: Allergy to casein or whey can cause reactions up to anaphylaxis.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Added maltose raises the total sugar level, which may be undesirable for diabetics.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Malted milk is more calorie‑dense than regular milk, so portion control is advised.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Malted milk can be enjoyed cold, blended into smoothies, added to porridge, baked goods, sauces, and desserts. It is often mixed into infant cereals to improve taste and energy content.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store malted milk in the refrigerator at 1‑4 °C. Once opened, consume within 5‑7 days. Do not freeze, as the texture may change.

potato-boiled-from-fresh-peel-not-eaten-.title: Boiled Potato, fresh, peel not eaten, no added fat

content.title: About
content.content: Boiled potato is a cooked tuber of the potato plant (Solanum tuberosum) prepared without added fat. The peel is not consumed, while the flesh retains most of the nutrients. Potato is a major source of carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals in many diets worldwide.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes were introduced to Europe from South America in the 16th century.
There are over 4,000 potato varieties differing in colour, shape, and taste.
Boiling preserves a large portion of vitamin C if the potatoes are not left in cold water for too long.
The peel contains more fiber and some vitamins, but it is omitted in this product.
Potato is one of the most widely consumed root vegetables in the world.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Boiled potato provides slow‑releasing energy, which helps maintain stable blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C acts as an antioxidant, supports the immune system, and aids collagen synthesis.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and supports heart and muscle function.

items.title: Provides dietary fiber
items.content: Even without the peel, the flesh contains some fiber that aids digestion.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: The absence of added fat makes this product suitable for low‑fat dietary plans.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Improperly stored or sprouted potatoes may contain solanine, a toxin that can cause nausea and headaches.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Boiled potatoes have a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion sizes.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Rarely, individuals may experience an allergic reaction to potatoes.

items.title: Potential contamination
items.content: Improper handling can lead to bacterial growth and foodborne illness.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Boiled potatoes can be eaten plain, added to salads, soups, mashed, or used as a filling. They can be sliced, cubed, or pureed. When serving, you may garnish with fresh herbs, spices, or a drizzle of olive oil.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store boiled potatoes in the refrigerator in an airtight container for up to 3–4 days. Allow them to cool completely before refrigerating. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags.

content.title: About
content.content: Potato soup is a classic dish made from boiled or stewed potatoes, broth, vegetables, and seasonings. It has a mild, slightly sweet flavor and a creamy texture when the potatoes are mashed.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Potatoes are the fourth most consumed food worldwide after rice, wheat, and corn.
Potato soup is popular in many cuisines: in Russia as "kartofelny sup", in France as "potage de pommes de terre", in Poland as "zupa ziemniaczana".
Potato soups are often prepared in colder months because they are warming and filling.
There are many variations: with cream, cheese, bacon, herbs, or carrots.
Potato soups can be clear broths or thick purées.

items.title: Rich in vitamin C
items.content: Potatoes provide vitamin C, which supports the immune system and collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Contains fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion and promotes satiety.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When prepared without cream or butter, the soup is low in fat, making it suitable for light diets.

items.title: Contains vitamin B6
items.content: Vitamin B6 is involved in protein metabolism and neurotransmitter synthesis.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: Adding too much salt can increase the risk of hypertension.

items.title: Potato allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to potatoes.

items.title: High glycemic index
items.content: Potatoes have a high glycemic index, so people with diabetes should monitor portion size.

items.title: Solanine content
items.content: Green parts and sprouted tubers contain solanine, a toxin that should be avoided.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve potato soup hot, often garnished with herbs (parsley, dill), croutons, or grated cheese. Cream can be added for extra richness, and spices such as black pepper, paprika, or bay leaf enhance flavor.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the cooked soup in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. When frozen, it keeps for up to 2 months; thaw in the refrigerator before reheating.
